title: Mechano-Node-Pore Sensing: A Rapid, Label-Free Platform for Multi-Parameter Single-Cell Viscoelastic Measurements
protocol: Design the width of the sizing and recovery segments wider than the largest cells but with sufficient signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
Choose the contraction segment width to apply a 30%-40% strain to the average cell size for mechanophenotyping.
Calculate strain using the formula imgsrc://cloudfront.jove.com/files/ftp_upload/64665/64665eq01.jpg, where d is cell diameter and wc is contraction channel width.
Design separate device geometries for different cell types or conditions with varying diameters.
Create a reference device for each unique device geometry to determine De, the effective sizing pore segment diameter.
Design and create a photomask with electrodes for microfluidic device current measurement.
Spin coat, pattern, and process a positive photoresist onto a plain glass slide according to the product data sheet.
Perform metal deposition of 75 Å Ti, 250 Å Pt, and 250 Å Au onto the slide using electron-gun evaporation.
Immerse the slide in acetone for 15 min to perform lift-off of excess metal.
Use a disposable pipette to drop-cast gold etchant onto the region of electrodes that will be exposed to the microfluidic channel.
Rinse the slide with deionized (DI) water.
Dry the slide with dry nitrogen (N2).
Score the slide along the patterned electrode boundaries using a glass cutting tool.
Break the glass along the score to partition the slide into individual chips.
Visually inspect the electrodes under a microscope.
Spin coat SU-8 epoxy resist onto a polished silicon wafer according to the product data sheet.
Measure feature heights using a profilometer.
Visually inspect the features under a microscope.
Ensure that the desired geometries are well-defined.
Weigh an elastomer and a crosslinker at a 10:1 mass ratio in a disposable cup for PDMS preparation.
Mix the PDMS vigorously for 30 s with a disposable fork until it is opaque with bubbles.
De-gas the PDMS in a vacuum chamber for approximately 30-90 minutes or until it becomes transparent and bubble-free.
Place the wafer with the SU-8 master mold into a disposable Petri dish.
Pour PDMS over the center of the wafer.
Place the Petri dish containing the PDMS and wafer in a vacuum chamber and de-gas for approximately 30 minutes or until no bubbles remain in the PDMS.
Bake the PDMS at 80 °C for 2 hours in an oven or on a hot plate.
Cut and remove the PDMS from the SU-8 negative master using a sharp blade.
Dice the molded PDMS slab into individual molds using a sharp blade.
Core the inlet and outlet access holes using a disposable biopsy punch.
Clean the electrode glass slides with methanol (≥99.8%).
Dry the glass slides with dry N2.
Clean the PDMS device with scotch tape, followed by a rinse with isopropyl alcohol (IPA) and deionized water (DI; 18 M/cm²).
Dry the PDMS device with dry N2.
Clean the PDMS device with scotch tape once more.
Place the glass substrate with prefabricated electrodes and the prepared PDMS mold (feature side up) into a plasma cleaner.
Expose both PDMS mold and glass substrate to oxygen plasma for 2 min.
Align and place the plasma-treated PDMS mold onto the glass substrate with prefabricated electrodes.
Pipette 20 µL of a 2:1 methanol in DI water dilution onto the plasma-treated glass surface, if alignment adjustments are needed.
Bake the aligned device at 50 °C for 2 h to evaporate the methanol solution and complete bonding, if methanol was used.
Visually inspect the bonded microfluidic device under a microscope to ensure proper alignment of electrodes and channel geometries.
Prepare the pressure source, PCB, benchtop hardware, and data acquisition software.
Connect the microfluidic device to the PCB using the clamp.
Align the spring-loaded pins on the clamp with the electrode contact pads on the microfluidic device.
Align the header pins on the clamp with the holes on the PCB.
Firmly insert the clamp's header pins into the PCB holes, ensuring that the spring-loaded pins remain aligned with the electrode contact pads.
Set up and connect the electronic hardware.
Connect two of the power supply's output ports to the PCB's supply voltage port with a double banana plug-to-BNC female adapter and a BNC cable.
Turn on the power supply.
Set the output connected to the BNC’s inner conductor to +15 V.
Set the other output to -15 V.
Enable both outputs to power the circuit.
Connect the third of the power supply's output ports to the input voltage port of the PCB with a BNC cable.
Set the output to the desired applied voltage, but do not enable it until starting the experiment.
Connect the PCB’s output current port to the input of the current preamplifier with a BNC cable.
Connect the output of the current preamplifier to one analog input on the BNC terminal block of the data acquisition system with a BNC cable.
Optionally, connect an analog low-pass filter in line with the BNC cable to filter out high-frequency interference.
Install and set up the required software on the personal computer (PC).
Power on and connect the pressure controller to the PC.
Install any required pressure controller software as per the manufacturer's instructions.
Install MATLAB on the PC.
Install the Data Acquisition Toolbox on the PC.
Ensure required drivers for the data acquisition system are installed.
Download the "NPS.m" script from GitHub.
Open and configure the downloaded data acquisition script.
Set correct values to initialize the data acquisition session.
Specify Vendor ID, Device ID, and analog input channel number in the script.
Set sample rate at least 10 kHz for optimal results.
Prepare a solution of 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS) in 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Filter the prepared FBS-PBS solution with a 0.22 µm filter.
Culture and prepare cells according to appropriate cell-culture protocol.
Suspend cells in 2% FBS-PBS at a concentration of 1-5 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Keep suspended cells on ice throughout experiments.
Load the cell sample into PTFE tubing.
Connect tubing containing cell sample to device inlet.
Cut 30 cm of PTFE tubing with a razor blade or sharp knife.
Attach one end of the tubing to a luer lock syringe.
Use the syringe to draw up the cell sample into the other end of the tubing.
Carefully insert the tubing into the inlet of the device.
Connect the opposite end of the tubing to the microfluidic pressure controller.
Set the desired constant driving pressure on the pressure controller software and allow the sample to fill the device.
Plug the device outlet and apply a low pressure to the inlet if bubbles form in the microfluidic channels.
Dislodge debris by lightly pressing on the top of the PDMS device while applying the driving pressure or toggling the pressure on and off if debris clogs the channel.
Switch to a new device if debris remains after attempting to dislodge it.
Set the desired voltage by rotating the Voltage knob on the power supply.
Enable the voltage by pressing the On button.
Set the voltage for data acquisition.
Turn on the current preamplifier and set sensitivity as low as possible or gain as high as possible without overloading.
Press the green Run button in MATLAB ribbon menu to start NPS.m script.
Begin sampling and saving data.
Press the Stop button in figure window to stop data acquisition script.
Disable power supply output by pressing the On button.
Set pressure source to zero pressure in pressure controller software.
Unclamp the device from the PCB and examine the channel's condition under a microscope.
Use new devices to measure cells of different types or conditions to avoid sample cross-contamination.
Apply gentle pressure to the syringe plunger to keep the cell sample at the very end of the tubing while inserting it into the device inlet.
Measure polystyrene beads in reference devices for calibration, choosing bead sizes smaller than the sizing channel.
Add 1.5% Tween and polystyrene beads to the filtered PBS and FBS solution used during cell experiments.
Proceed with the experiment using the reference device described in step 1.3 and apply the same voltage used during experimentation.
Use the average magnitude of the current drop produced as beads transit the sizing pores for calibration.
Calculate De, using the known diameter of the beads and the average magnitude of the current drop.
Measure the average size of cells in the sample using a commercially available instrument.
Analyze data to extract cell phenotypes.
Preprocess the data.
Compute the measured electrical current by applying the gain value used in the current-to-voltage preamplifier to the raw data acquired by the DAQ.
Remove high-frequency noise by applying a rectangular smoothing function and/or a low-pass filter to the raw current measurement.
Resample the filtered data to a lower sample rate.
Compute the corresponding timestamp data at this lower sample rate.
Compute a fitted baseline current signal using asymmetric least-squares smoothing.
Compute the approximate first derivative of the preprocessed current data by taking the difference between subsequent data points.
Identify cell events and extract subpulse data.
Search for candidate cell events by examining the preprocessed data.
Reject cell events that overlap with other cell events.
Reject cell events exhibiting a poor baseline fit.
Reject cell events with unexpected or erroneous pulse shapes.
Extract subpulse data for each accepted cell event.
Identify the start of each subpulse by computing the timepoint when the difference signal reaches a local minimum value.
Identify the end of each subpulse by computing the timepoint when the difference signal reaches a local maximum value.
Determine the width of each subpulse as the elapsed time between the start and end time points.
Determine the amplitude of each subpulse by computing the mean of the difference between the measured current and the baseline current for all data points between the start and end time points.
Determine the cell mechanophenotype for each cell event based on subpulse data.
Determine the cell diameter d using the equation defined by Deblois and Bean.
Determine the fluid velocity Uflow by calculating the mean cell velocity in the sizing subpulses, using the known segment lengths and measured duration of each subpulse.
Identify the cell's recovery time from deformation as the first recovery subpulse with an amplitude within 8% of the mean amplitude from the sizing subpulse.
